title: Introduce econ-smelter CLI: tenant micro-simulator and heuristic export for batch/cache/quant profiles
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a lightweight way to reason about tenant-level unit economics (a simple, reproducible sandbox) before applying batch/cache/quantization defaults at scale. This PR adds a developer-facing CLI called "econ-smelter" that runs a Monte Carlo micro-simulator using a tenant's sampled traffic profile and produces deterministic heuristic presets (batch shapes, prefix cache hints, and candidate quant profiles) plus a provenance report that ties heuristics back to simulated cost/latency tradeoffs.

What this changes: single continuous change set that introduces: 1) cmd/econ-smelter CLI (Go) with subcommands `simulate`, `export-presets`, and `explain`; 2) a compact simulator implemented in Python (internal/econ/simulator.py) that can be embedded or run remotely for heavier sim runs; 3) heuristics generator (internal/econ/heuristics.go) that converts simulation results into tenant-safe presets with confidence bands; 4) telemetry adapter (internal/telemetry/econ_exporter.go) to emit structured events to Console for visual diffs; 5) a small presets-as-code YAML schema and examples under examples/econ-smelter/; 6) e2e smoke tests and unit tests.

Key behaviors and guarantees: - The CLI accepts either a recorded sample (ndjson of request shapes) or a synthetic distribution and runs N Monte Carlo trials to compute expected per-token cost, P95 latency, and fallback risk. - Heuristics generator produces up to three candidate presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and annotates them with expected unit cost delta and rollback safety score. - Exports include a normalized telemetry manifest so Console can visualize the simulated delta when importing a preset. - Default output is idempotent YAML that can be applied with existing defaults-as-code tooling.

How to review: focus on correctness of simulation maths (internal/econ/simulator.py), the mapping heuristics (internal/econ/heuristics.go), and the telemetry schema (internal/telemetry/econ_schema.md embedded). The PR includes an annotated example run in examples/econ-smelter/run-annotation.md.

Testing notes: included unit tests cover the mapping from simulation percentiles to preset thresholds and CLI integration tests exercise a small synthetic tenant trace. Local smoke run performed with `make econ-smelter-sample` reproduces the sample in examples and prints three preset candidates.

Performance: small-sample simulations (5k synthetic requests, 100 trials) complete in ~6s locally and in CI the Python sim is capped with a 30s timeout. Heuristic generation is O(n) in the number of candidate shapes and negligible.

Backward compatibility: presets produced use the current presets schema and will be validated against the existing presets-as-code validator. No runtime configuration has changed; this is an additive tooling feature.

Security: no secrets or keys are introduced. Telemetry events are scrubbed of request payloads; only shape/size/latency/cost statistics are emitted.

Release notes: new command-line tool `econ-smelter` (developer preview) for tenant-level microeconomic simulation and heuristics export.

Related: ENG-2148 (tenant prefilling simulation prototype), ENG-2199 (presets-as-code import path), and an internal doc link to the Console visualization PR (referenced in the review comments).

review_comments: Marco Li: Great direction. One question: the simulator assumes independent inter-arrival times per request — can we model burst correlations?

Elena Park: We kept the first pass simple to get an iterative flow. I added a `--burst-model` flag that accepts a small HMM descriptor; docs note the limitation. Will iterate if we see requests that need it.
Dina Rao: The rollback safety score is helpful; please add a short justification for the thresholds used (why 15% delta maps to 'balanced').
Elena Park: Added justification and links to ENG-2148 design notes in examples/run-annotation.md; thresholds come from historical tenant rollouts and conservative bounds used by the rollout service.
Owen Fitzgerald: CI flaked once on the Python sim timeout; can you ensure the sim has deterministic RNG seed for tests?
Elena Park: Test changes: sim_test uses fixed seed and CI config increased test timeout to 45s for Linux runners. Reran CI and all checks passed.
release_notes: Developer-preview: `econ-smelter` CLI for tenant micro-simulation and automated preset suggestions (batch/cache/quant). Use with presets-as-code import path to preview expected unit-econ deltas.
notes_for_prod_ops: This tool is developer-facing; no infra changes. If teams want to run large simulations in CI, they should call the python simulator in a dedicated job with increased timeout and resource limits. Telemetry events are tagged with `econ-smelter:v0` and can be filtered in Console.
